route.title: Superscription
route.marker: The doubled oracle and vision-book labels name the subject and seer before repeated Yahweh predicates begin at 1:2.
route.rationale: The paired genre notices complete a book threshold before the divine-character hymn opens, so the heading remains recoverable without pretending to develop the following oracle.
route.rejected: Merging 1:1 with 1:2-8 would hide the heading-to-hymn seam and turn framing metadata into the first hymnic predicate.
route.basis: The double superscription finishes before the repeated Yahweh clauses, making the heading a local unit inside the full first movement.
route.counter: The heading frames the whole book and is too brief to interpret independently without its book parent.
route.guard: No authorship, date, provenance, city identity, or canon ruling.

route.title: Theophanic hymn with refuge and judgment climax
route.marker: Repeated Yahweh attributes expand through storm, sea, river, mountain, world, and endurance questions before the good-refuge versus overflowing-end antithesis closes the movement.
route.rationale: Divine character, cosmic manifestation, human inability to stand, refuge, and enemy pursuit form one coherent hymn whose 1:7-8 contrast functions as its paired climax rather than a detached maxim.
route.rejected: Splitting 1:2-6 from 1:7-8 would make the positive-negative antithesis look independent of the avenging, slow-to-anger, and theophanic predicates that frame it.
route.basis: The complete hymn moves from divine predicates to cosmic effects and finally to the paired fates of refugees and enemies.
route.counter: The renewed good-refuge assertion at 1:7 is a real stanza pressure, and literary and canonical primaries favored a dependent 1:7-8 child.
route.guard: Never retrieve 1:7 alone; possible acrostic pressure is evidence only, with no reconstruction or emendation.

route.title: Adversary plot indictment and consumption verdict
route.marker: The plotting question and repeated full-end claim lead through thorn, drunkenness, and dry-stubble images to the wicked counselor emerging from the addressed city; WLC samekh follows 1:11.
route.rationale: Challenge, total-end verdict, consumption imagery, and identification of hostile counsel complete one accusatory address before the Thus-says formula resets the discourse at 1:12.
route.rejected: Extending the unit through 1:14 would cross the marked 1:11 closure and absorb the paired release-and-doom decree into the plot indictment.
route.basis: The question, verdict, illustrative images, and wicked-counselor identification are bounded by the WLC paragraph mark.
route.counter: The full-end phrase links backward to 1:8, and feminine address at 1:11 does not resolve the historical identity of the target.
route.guard: Pronouns and historical identities remain undecided; hydrate 1:9-15 for address context.

route.title: Paired release and hostile-doom oracle
route.marker: Thus says Yahweh at 1:12 governs adversary removal and release from yoke; Yahweh has commanded concerning you at 1:14 turns to name, cult objects, grave, and vileness before a WLC pe.
route.rationale: Release of the afflicted addressee and extinction of the hostile name are deliberately juxtaposed as a paired reversal inside the section bounded by the samekh after 1:11 and pe after 1:14.
route.rejected: Splitting 1:12-13 from 1:14 would honor the renewed formula but weaken the paired oppressor-removal and delivered-community reversal that the paragraph closure holds together.
route.basis: The two addressee fates work as one reversal and the WLC paragraph closes only after the hostile decree.
route.counter: The gender and addressee shift at 1:14 is genuine; literary and canonical primaries treated the hostile decree as independently recoverable.
route.guard: Do not assign fixed historical identities from English pronouns; preserve the internal 1:13|1:14 seam.

route.title: Mountain herald and festival proclamation
route.marker: Behold introduces the mountain herald; peace announcement, explicit Judah address, feast and vow imperatives, and the wicked one cut off complete the proclamation; WEB 1:15 equals WLC 2:1.
route.rationale: Announcement, named audience, cultic imperatives, and their enemy-removal rationale form a complete herald speech after the pe following WEB and WLC 1:14.
route.rejected: Merging with 1:12-14 would absorb Judah's proclamation into the hostile decree, while merging with 2:1-2 would confuse its audience with the besieged city.
route.basis: The behold formula, explicit addressee, imperatives, and reason make a complete proclamation across a versification-only chapter seam.
route.counter: The verse realizes the preceding hostile termination and forms a contrast with the attacker alarm that follows.
route.guard: Never retrieve without 1:9-15 and the WEB 1:15/WLC 2:1 disclosure; later good-news wording is context only.

route.title: Attacker alarm and restoration counterstatement
route.marker: The attacker's arrival triggers four defense imperatives, and the causal for in 2:2 supplies the restoration counterstatement after prior devastation.
route.rationale: Alarm and causal rationale make a concise paired opening: 2:2 explains the literary function of the attack warning and cannot safely become a detached restoration claim.
route.rejected: Absorbing 2:1-2 into the detailed tableau beginning at 2:3 would hide the imperative-and-rationale threshold before shields and chariots take over.
route.basis: The defense commands and causal restoration statement are mutually interpreting before the visual siege sequence begins.
route.counter: The besieged addressee in 2:1 and Jacob-Israel in 2:2 differ, while attacker imagery continues into 2:3.
route.guard: Never surface 2:2 alone; hydrate 2:1-13 and make no battle chronology claim.

route.title: Siege, breach, flight, plunder, and desolation tableau
route.marker: Red shields, flashing chariots, rushing troops, river gates, palace collapse, carrying away, flight, plunder commands, and the empty-void-waste triad progress without leaving the siege scene.
route.rationale: Military preparation, assault, breach, deportation, flight, plunder, and bodily terror are sequential phases of one accelerating collapse tableau whose outcome is reached at 2:10.
route.rejected: Splitting 2:3-7 from 2:8-10 would recognize the move from breach to aftermath, but both children require the same attack-to-desolation action and mandatory whole-scene hydration.
route.basis: The kinetic sequence continues from preparation through the terminal desolation formula without a new oracle frame.
route.counter: Nahum 2:7 is syntactically difficult, and 2:8 names Nineveh while shifting to flight and plunder; the Hebrew primary favored two dependent scene children.
route.guard: Keep 2:7 inside the whole 2:3-10 tableau; translation questions about its subject have no boundary authority.

route.title: Lion-den taunt and divine verdict
route.marker: The Where-is question opens sustained lion, cub, den, kill, and prey imagery; Behold, I am against you answers by destroying chariots, young lions, prey, and messengers before the WLC samekh.
route.rationale: The direct first-person verdict extinguishes each element of the lion boast and therefore completes, rather than merely follows, the taunt.
route.rejected: Detaching 2:13 would honor its divine-speech formula but sever the verdict from the metaphor and rhetorical question it resolves.
route.basis: Question, boast, and answering verdict close together at the WLC paragraph marker.
route.counter: The renewed direct-divine formula gives 2:13 real standalone pressure inside the larger unit.
route.guard: Never retrieve the verdict without the lion-den taunt; make no national or violence-ethics ruling.

route.title: Bloody-city woe, battle register, and causal charge
route.marker: Woe names the city; whip, wheels, horses, chariots, sword, spear, and bodies build the battle soundscape; because in 3:4 supplies the stated causal accusation.
route.rationale: The vivid assault register is syntactically and rhetorically completed by its because-clause, so woe, casualties, and charge remain one indictment.
route.rejected: Extending through 3:7 would erase the renewed direct-opposition formula and first-person exposure actions at 3:5.
route.basis: The battle catalogue requires its causal accusation, and the direct-divine verdict begins only at 3:5.
route.counter: The cause in 3:4 directly grounds the 3:5-7 sentence, and the Hebrew primary preferred the complete 3:1-7 charge-verdict oracle.
route.guard: Never surface 3:2-3 apart from the woe and causal charge; make no detached violence or identity claim.

route.title: Direct exposure and shame oracle
route.marker: Behold, I am against you begins serial first-person exposure actions, followed by spectators' flight, their waste verdict, and the no-mourner and no-comforter close.
route.rationale: The renewed speaker formula, first-person actions, public reaction, and abandonment questions create a clear oracle after the causal charge in 3:4.
route.rejected: Merging 3:1-7 would preserve accusation and sentence together but hide the 3:5 speaker-and-form reset that makes the exposure oracle locally recoverable.
route.basis: The direct-opposition formula creates a new speech form while the larger 3:1-7 parent preserves causality.
route.counter: This unit remains causally dependent on 3:1-4, and the Hebrew primary treated the whole 3:1-7 as one charge-verdict movement.
route.guard: Hydrate 3:1-7; do not isolate sexualized exposure imagery or infer general identity or ethics rules.

route.title: No-Amon comparison and matching verdict
route.marker: Are you better than No-Amon opens the example; waters and allies establish strength, yet recounts captivity, and you also applies the comparison at 3:11.
route.rationale: Example, narrated outcome, and direct inference are inseparable: the comparison cannot stand without the fall, and the verdict cannot stand without the comparison.
route.rejected: Splitting 3:8-10 from 3:11 would detach the you-also application that states why the comparison was introduced.
route.basis: The applied verdict explicitly completes the comparison before fortress imagery begins at 3:12.
route.counter: The direct second-person prediction at 3:11 is a local voice shift and 3:12 continues the same address.
route.guard: Keep comparison and inference together; No-Amon identity, history, and chronology remain unadjudicated.

route.title: Fortress-futility and locust taunt
route.marker: Ripe-fig fortresses, opened gates, ironic siege-preparation imperatives, fire and sword, multiplying merchants, and disappearing locust-like guards and officials accumulate through 3:17.
route.rationale: Exposed defenses, frantic preparation, consuming consequence, multiplication, and disappearance form one cumulative futility taunt whose insect bridge begins in 3:15.
route.rejected: Splitting 3:12-15 from 3:16-17 would distinguish fortress preparation from merchant and official imagery but interrupt the multiply-then-vanish locust reversal.
route.basis: The locust bridge carries the preparation verdict into the commercial and administrative disappearance taunt.
route.counter: Nahum 3:16 changes the referents from siege preparation to merchants, guards, and officials; literary and canonical primaries favored that child seam.
route.guard: Hydrate the full 3:12-17 taunt; locust lexemes and roots are evidence only and no gloss is total meaning.

route.title: Leader lament, incurable wound, and hearers' response
route.marker: The vocative king of Assyria introduces sleeping shepherds, fallen nobles, and scattered people; incurable wound, universal handclapping, and the final question close the book.
route.rationale: Leadership collapse, communal scattering, fatal injury, outside response, and closing question form the terminal royal lament-coda.
route.rejected: Attaching 3:18-19 to 3:12-17 would keep institutional collapse together but conceal the explicit royal vocative and final lament form.
route.basis: The royal vocative opens the final address and the incurable-wound question closes it.
route.counter: Verse 19 broadens from internal collapse to hearers' reaction while retaining the same second-person wound address.
route.guard: Never surface 3:19 as detached celebration; keep 3:18-19 and hydrate 3:8-19 with a violence-ethics caution.

dissents.rationale: Literary and canonical primaries preserve the refuge-versus-overflow antithesis as possible dependent children; the boss retained the complete hymn.
The renewed decree and addressee shift at 1:14 support a dependent child; paragraph closure after 1:14 favors the paired outer unit.
The Hebrew primary preserves attack-breach and flight-plunder children; the boss retained the whole siege tableau.
The Hebrew primary preserves the whole charge-verdict oracle; the boss accepted the 3:5 direct-speech reset with mandatory parent hydration.
Literary and canonical primaries preserve a merchant-and-official child seam at 3:16; the boss retained the cumulative fortress-to-locust taunt.
WEB 2:7/WLC 2:8 subject and syntax remain a translation-hydration question with no boundary impact.
The locust terms in 3:15-17 remain a lexical-hydration question with no boundary impact; roots are not total meaning.
